title: Air-gapped Control Plane: setup & maintenance playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for installing and operating the private control plane in air-gapped / VPC-on-prem environments. Focus areas: initial bootstrap, Terraform handoff patterns, capacity scaling, KMS/certificate rotation, and safe upgrade recipes (canary/rollback).

Scope / assumptions:
- Target: Private control plane (API + control services) behind customer-managed network (no egress to public internet) or limited egress via approved proxy.
- Kubernetes-based control plane (k8s 1.26+) and Postgres (managed by customer or our optional operator).
- Terraform used for infra + k8s manifests (module pattern described below).
- Customers may require HSM/KMS integration, compliance logging, and long retention for observability.

High-level flow (initial setup):
1) Preflight checklist (network & infra):
   - Confirm subnets for control-plane nodes (three AZs recommended for HA).
   - NAT or proxy for required package sources (if air-gapped, mirror images into local registry).
   - Internal DNS entries: controlplane.redwood.local (A records for load balancer).
   - TLS cert plan: does customer provide certs or do we generate CSR to be signed? (decide up front).
   - Firewall rules: ports 443/8443, 22 (ops), metrics ports 9090/9100 restricted to monitoring CIDRs.

2) Bootstrap order (minimal interrupt):
   - Provision VMs/network via terraform-module:network
   - Provision storage (CSI-backed PV class) and Postgres storage
   - Apply k8s control-plane manifests (namespace, CRDs, operators)
   - Deploy core services (auth, config-store, api-gateway) with non-zero replicas for HA
   - Smoke tests: health endpoints, API token exchange, simple generate request to local model shim.

Terraform module notes (practical patterns):
- Module boundaries we use: network, vm-pool, dns, k8s-bootstrap, postgres-operator, controlplane-helm
- Keep k8s manifests templated and applied via helm_release in terraform where possible to keep single deployment pipeline. Avoid mixing kubectl apply pipelines in prod-runbooks unless explicitly documented.
- Inputs to watch: node_pool_size (default 3), instance_type, etcd_disk_size_gb, pg_replica_count.
- Outputs to capture in state: controlplane_lb_ip, kubeconfig_secret_location, pg_primary_endpoint.
- Remote state: insist on object-store (S3/MinIO) with state-locking (DynamoDB or Consul). In air-gapped sites use customer-provided MinIO endpoint + etcd lock service.
- Example minimal module invocation (notes, not copy/paste-tested):
   module "network" {
     source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//network"
     vpc_cidr = var.vpc_cidr
   }

- Migration note: when changing module outputs used by downstream modules, always add a staged deploy where old output remains for one release to avoid terraform destroying dependent resources.

Upgrade plan (control plane version bumps):
- Versioning: tag releases as cp-v<major>.<minor>.<patch>. Upgrade window set in calendar with customer.
- Canary strategy (recommended):
  1) Spin up a canary control-plane in parallel using canary namespace + LB (same infra but separate k8s namespace).
  2) Route 5% of test traffic (internal) and run e2e smoke/fuzz tests for 4 hours.
  3) If green, roll to remaining replicas via rolling update.
- Blue/Green (for breaking DB migrations):
  - Provision green cluster + run migrations against replica DB (replica promoted only after successful validation).
  - Switch traffic at LB level, keep blue available for 24h for quick rollback.
- Rollback plan: keep previous Helm chart/manifest tarballs in artifacts bucket. For terraform-driven infra changes, have a documented state rollback procedure (restore remote state snapshot).

KMS / key rotation steps (customer HSM/KMS):
- Inventory keys used: signing-cert, tls-cp, db-encryption-key, artifact-signing-key (list in secure vault).
- Rotation pattern: 
  1) Create new key in KMS.
  2) Configure control plane to accept both old+new keys (dual-read) and deploy a hot-patch.
  3) Re-encrypt artifacts DB (if applicable) with new key using background job.
  4) After 48h and verification, retire old key via KMS policy.
- If HSM-backed, ensure ops window and physical presence matches customer's policy.

Certificate rotation (TLS):
- CSR generation: use the CSR helper script under tools/cert-gen.sh (mirror into airgapped environment).
- Rolling TLS update: one replica at a time, wait for readiness, then move to next. For single-replica deployments, require brief maintenance window.

Scaling runbook (horizontal / vertical):
- Autoscaling: we recommend cluster-autoscaler for worker pools; control-plane services use HPA with conservative cpu/mem thresholds.
- Manual scale steps (fast path):
  - Terraform change: increase node_pool_size -> terraform apply -> watch node readiness
  - Redis/KV cache warming: after scale up, run cache-warm job (payloads in tools/cache-warm/).
- Sizing heuristics (initial guidance):
  - Small (dev): 3 x m5.large-equivalent, 8 CPU / 32GB RAM each for small throughput
  - Prod starter: 5 x m5.4xlarge-equivalent, 16 CPU / 128GB RAM each (depends heavily on expected concurrency and model sizes)
  - Latency-sensitive: add headroom for CPU-bound transformer ops and consider model quantization to reduce memory.
- Sharding and model variants: prefer routing policy that pins heavy models to dedicated node pools to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

Maintenance & rotation checklist (brief):
- Weekly:
  - Check Postgres replication lag < 500ms
  - Check prometheus node health and scrape coverage
  - Rotate access keys older than 90 days
- Monthly:
  - KMS key inventory review
  - Disk IO metrics review and PV reclamation check
- Before any upgrade:
  - Snapshot remote terraform state
  - Database backup + logical dump (store in customer-provided object store)
  - Confirm rollback runbook and contact list (customer oncall + Redwood SRE PM)

Operational troubleshooting (common scenarios):
- Control plane partially unreachable:
  1) Check LB health -> if >50% nodes unhealthy, scale node pool to 0->N to force fresh nodes.
  2) Check etcd/consul leader status (k8s endpoints).
  3) If DB unreachable, promote read-replica after ensuring WAL shipping is intact.
- Load spike causing 5xxs:
  - Reduce allowed model concurrency via feature flag for that customer; enable fallback model variant.
  - Throttle non-critical background jobs.
- Terraform drift: run 'terraform plan' in CI against a non-destructive check; if drift present, annotate and plan small corrective patch.

Testing & validation (pre-go-live):
- Acceptance tests: smoke, canary load (10% of expected sustained RPS for 30m), failover test (simulate AZ loss).
- Security: ensure mTLS between services where required; run dependency scanning in airgapped registry.
- Performance: token-per-second measurements with sample prompt sets (store results in artifacts).

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: define minimal set of metrics that must be forwarded to Redwood Console when customer opts-in (metrics namespace + retention).
- Q: Should we provide a built-in object-store shim for remote-state in fully air-gapped installs (MinIO+etcd) or rely on customer's S3? (Priya to decide)
- TODO: add post-upgrade smoke script to terraform-modules repo and reference from here.
- Note: Need to reconcile this playbook with onprem-private-init-scale-rotation-playbook-draft (some overlap) — we should consolidate common sequences and keep one canonical.

Appendix: quick commands & helpful links
- Bootstrap example (ops machine inside customer net):
  # fetch mirrored terraform modules
  git clone --depth=1 git@github.com:redwood/terraform-modules.git /opt/terraform-modules
  cd /opt/terraform-modules/examples/controlplane-airgap
  export TF_VAR_vpc_cidr=10.10.0.0/16
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=minio-cp-state" -backend-config="endpoint=https://minio.internal"
  terraform plan
  terraform apply -auto-approve

- Useful diagnostics:
  kubectl get pods -n redwood --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
  kubectl describe pod <pod> -n redwood
  curl -sS https://controlplane.local/healthz | jq

- Reference artifacts:
  - GH PR: https://github.com/redwood/terraform-modules/pull/42 (sane defaults for controlplane module)
  - Jira: ENG-2345 (airgap module backlog)

If you are reading this and have ops run experience in a tired datacenter: please add step-by-step commands you used (especially for MinIO init, network proxy configuration, and KMS HSM handshake steps).

Revision history: draft v0.1 (2025-01-10) initial notes by Maya; v0.2 (2025-02-18) added canary/blue-green guidance and terraform module patterns.
